subject: Computer Networking
title: IMAP — Syncing Mail
description: A short lesson to help you apply IMAP — Syncing Mail.

hook.text: Open email on your phone, then on your laptop. Same inbox, same read flags. IMAP does that.

buildup.text: IMAP keeps all email on the server. Your client syncs a view — folders, flags, and messages.

discovery.text: Mark a message as read on one device. IMAP syncs that flag to every other device automatically.

twist.text: IMAP uses server storage for everything. Delete old mail or buy more storage when it fills up.

climax.text: IDLE command lets the server push new mail instantly. No polling delay — real-time notifications.

punchline.text: IMAP syncs your inbox everywhere. One source of truth.

quiz.question: Where does IMAP store your emails?
options: On the server, synced to all devices
Only on the first device that downloads them
In a local file on each device independently

details.summary: Internet Message Access Protocol keeps email on the server and synchronizes it across multiple devices. IMAP lets you read, organize, and search email from your phone, laptop, and desktop while keeping everything in sync.
details.whyItMatters: IMAP enables the multi-device email experience everyone expects today. Without IMAP, reading email on your phone would not update your laptop.
takeaways: IMAP stores email on the server, not the local device
It synchronizes read status, folders, and flags across devices
IMAP replaced POP3 for multi-device email access

faq.question: How does IMAP keep devices in sync?
faq.answer: IMAP stores all messages and their state on the server. When you read, move, or delete a message on one device, the change is reflected on the server. Other devices see the updated state when they sync. The server is the single source of truth.

faq.question: Does IMAP use more server storage than POP3?
faq.answer: Yes. POP3 typically downloads messages and deletes them from the server. IMAP keeps everything on the server indefinitely. This requires more server storage but provides the sync and search capabilities that modern email users expect across all their devices.
